Hi Emily / NovaCorp team,

Thanks again for the call last week. I pulled together the usage and perf evidence for Q1–Q2 so we can align on renewal options with concrete numbers before procurement jumps in. Attached: Q1–Q2 usage report (token breakdown by model and route) and a short latency snapshot. Key highlights: 

- Net token consumption (Jan–May): 48.3M tokens (customer-generated + assistant).
- 60% of tokens come from our high-throughput embedding route; chat generation accounts for most of the p95 latency variance.
- Observed spike on 2026-05-18 — a model upgrade changed batching behavior, increasing p95 by ~120ms for a 3-hour window; overall p95 remained within 800–950ms.

Optionally useful next steps I recommend:
- Short SLA addendum (SLO: 99th <= 1.2s for chat, 95th <= 600ms for embeddings) + credit schedule.
- A 6–12 month term with a capacity uplift (reserve pool) to stabilize throughput and reduce unit cost.
- Pilot for dedicated GPU pool for a single route (2–4 weeks) to validate latency improvements before committing.

Could you loop in your procurement contact and let me know whether NovaCorp prefers a shorter bridge term or a full 12-month commit? I can prepare two concrete proposals once I hear which direction you'd like (bridge vs. term).

Team — quick internal note before we respond to Emily/procurement. Thoughts below.

Summary of ask: NovaCorp wants a 9-month bridge with a discount and a simple SLO credit table; they also want uplift pricing for a reserved pool pilot.

Suggested response options (pick one):

Option A — Bridge (recommended):
- 9-month bridge with 20% capacity uplift (guaranteed reserved vCPU/GPU slots scaled to their peak day)
- 5% one-time term discount on usage rates for the bridge period
- SLO credit schedule: 5% credit for p95 > 1.2s (chat) for a monthly window; 3% for p95 > 1.4s (escalating).
- Offer a 2-week dedicated pilot with no charge for the first week (burst credit) so they can validate latency gains.

Option B — 12-month commit:
- 12-month term with tiered discounts (7% at sign, additional 3% after hitting 60% consumption)
- Lower unit price but longer lock-in; pilot still included as a paid 50% discount trial week.

Technical notes to include in response:
- Root cause of 5/18 spike: model parameter packing changed batching thresholds; we rolled a config tweak that reverted to prior behavior within ~3 hours. No errors or timeouts were observed at the Redwood edge, but downstream retries were visible in NovaCorp telemetry (likely due to backoff-triggered retries). We can include the packet traces if procurement requests them.

Pricing docs: I tossed a draft addendum (pricing v1) in the thread attachments. Rishi — can you confirm the uplift pricing numbers for a 20% reserved pool bump and the credit math? Naomi — please confirm SLA credit phrasing (keep it simple).

If we agree on Option A internally, Jordan can send a clean single-page proposal + addendum to Emily and procurement.

Thanks for the quick feedback. Below is a consolidated, actionable proposal that hits NovaCorp's asks while giving you an easy path to evaluate latency improvements.

What happened (brief):
- On 2026-05-18 a model packaging change altered batching thresholds; this increased p95 for chat for ~3 hours. We reverted the config and pushed a follow-up optimization the next day. No 5xx errors or service interruptions from Redwood's side; observed downstream retries likely due to client backoff settings. Happy to share traces with your SREs if useful.

Our proposal (Option A — 9-month bridge):
- Term: 9 months starting on sign.
- Capacity: 20% reserved uplift (monthly committed capacity; reduces per-token unit price).
- Pricing: 5% one-time discount applied to usage rates during the 9-month bridge (see draft_addendum_pricing_v1.pdf).
- SLO / Credit: Simple table attached (SLO credit table in draft addendum). Example: monthly credit of 5% for p95 chat > 1.2s, 1% for p95 chat between 1.0–1.2s, maximum 15% credit per quarter.
- Pilot: 2-week dedicated pool pilot — first week free (burst credits) to validate latency; second week discounted at 50% of uplift cost. Pilot scope: one chat route + one embedding route.

Attached: pricing addendum draft, SLO snapshot, usage evidence. Next steps if this looks good:
1) Let me know procurement's preferred sign date window (we can retro-start the bridge to align with billing cycle).
2) I'll schedule the pilot kickoff for the week after sign and send a one-page proposal for signature.
3) If you'd like traces for the 5/18 spike, tell me who on your SRE team to share with and we'll send the packet/trace bundle.
